messages.subject: granularity of pull requests (was Re: [math] Feature/issue 202 vectorize all (#240))
parts:
[issue discussion spinning out to stan-dev]

The issue of how granular we should make pull requests keeps
coming up. But we have competing goals. On the one hand, a pull
request should be a complete unit of functionality. On the other
hand, it should be small, so that it's relatively easy to review.

We've been having a discussion on this particular Math lib issue,
but we don't have a general resolution. I was proposing we put
in the pull request for the infrastructure, then follow it up
with pull requests for applications (in this case, the infrastructure
is all the template programs to do vectorization and the application
is the vectorization of our unary functions).

The vectorization of unary functions can then itself be in two stages.
One to update the math lib, another to add them to the Stan language.

That's what I propose, but what do other people think in terms of
granularity of pull requests?

- Bob

for development and integration — add feature,
propagate changes in stages, deprecate any
